svg.text: User Journey: Lightweight Foldable Mobility Scooter
Elderly riders and their family caregivers · synthesized from 36 in-depth interviews (China) · a case study in user research and product definition
Age 55–88 (median 76). Walks short distances, uses a scooter for
errands and strolls. Wants independence, dislikes anything that
Usually an adult child, often living in another city. Buys for
safety and peace of mind; often the one who lifts the scooter
The scooter gives the rider freedom every day, yet becomes a burden at the moments of lifting, travel and repair, and those moments decide whether the family
1–2 h a day, mostly on flat,

Stage 6 (lift & carry) and stage 7 (travel) have the lowest emotion and the highest unmet need, so weight, fold size and compliance are the launch wedge. Stage 4 and stage 8 are the next fixes.
Percentages are shares of the interview sample (n=36) and are directional. Quotes are paraphrased and anonymized. Evidence level: interview-based, not a statistical study.
